news.title: 2014 World Cup Top Scorer Rodriguez Retires from Colombia National Football Team
news.lede: ▲ James Rodriguez playing for the Colombia national team James Rodriguez (35), a symbol of Colombian football, has concluded his illustrious 15-year career with the national team. In a video posted on his social media on the 16th (Korean time), Rodriguez announced his retirement from international football, saying, "Thank you for every match, every joy and tear, and every dream we shared together. Wearing the Colombia national team jersey and representing my country has been the greatest honor of my life." Making his senior national team debut for Colombia in 2011, Rodriguez has made a total of 131 A-international appearances, scoring 31 goals and providing 43 assists, while participating in three World Cups and four Copa Americas.

news.title: 2014 World Cup top scorer James Rodriguez has retired from the Colombian national team
news.lede: James Rodriguez, the 2014 World Cup's top scorer, has retired from the Colombian national team, the player announced this on his Instagram page, APA reports. "Thank you for every game, every joy, every tear, and every shared happiness. Defending the colors of the Colombian national team is one of the greatest honors of my life," Rodriguez wrote.

news.title: Why Lionel Messi is in Argentina squad weeks after announcing retirement
news.lede: Messi announced at the end of August that he is retiring from international football, ending a glittering 21-year spell for his country. His news came just weeks after Argentina lost 1-0 against Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. Club football pauses for the first international break of the 2026/27 season, which will last three weeks, towards the end of this month. Argentina have three fixtures lined up and, despite his decision to call time with his nation, Messi will feature in the coming weeks.

news.title: Africa’s Last Hope Arrives: Falconets Land in Bielsko-Biała for England World Cup Showdown
news.lede: Nigeria’s Falconets have arrived in Bielsko-Biała ahead of their crucial Round of 16 encounter against England at the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, carrying not only the country’s hopes but also Africa’s remaining challenge at the tournament. Moses Aduku’s side will face the Young Lionesses on Thursday for a place in the quarter-finals after recovering from a difficult start to qualify from Group F. Nigeria are the only African team remaining in the competition, with Ghana, Tanzania and Benin all failing to progress beyond the group stage. The Falconets reached the knockout phase in spectacular fashion, recording a historic 10-1 victory over New Caledonia in their final group match.

news.title: 'It was the moment' - Tuchel reveals bizarre World Cup regret
news.lede: The Three Lions’ 3-2 victory over the co-hosts in July was one of the tournament’s most enthralling matches. Two goals from Jude Bellingham and a Harry Kane penalty was enough for ten-man England to see off a second-half Mexican onslaught. The win was made all the more impressive due to the match being played 2,240 metres above sea level – a condition that Tuchel's men were not physically conditioned for. The German sat down with Daniel Sturridge in ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’ - to be released on Wednesday - to reflect on the eventful night in Mexico City and revealed his one regret, albeit a slightly bizarre one.

news.title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup
news.lede: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year. The 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out. Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona) Segura is no stranger to knockout football, having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantle again as La Roja eased through their group.
